category.title: Calves
category.intro: Programmes that strengthen your calf muscles, Achilles tendon and the front of your shins. You start with calf raises on the floor and progress to the step, single-leg work and hops.
science: Working calf raises with the heel down, that is with the muscle in a stretched position, was the method that increased muscle growth most in an 8-week study; that's why dropping the heel below the step is valuable.
With the knee bent, the big calf muscle works less and the one beneath it relatively more; the difference is small, so both positions are used together.
Calf raises with a slow lowering phase are the basis of the programmes recommended for the Achilles tendon.
Because the calves work constantly in daily life they are very enduring; to grow, sets need to go until they're truly tired.

exercises.name: Calf Raise
exercises.setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart. You can hold a wall lightly for balance.
steps: Rise up onto your toes by lifting your heels.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your calves.
Lower your heels slowly to the floor.
exercises.tip: Keep your weight between your big toe and second toe.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your ankle roll outwards.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.setup: Stand on one foot and lift the other slightly behind you. Support yourself with one hand on a wall.
steps: Rise up onto your toes.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly; switch legs halfway through.
exercises.tip: Try it once you can do 25 reps comfortably on two legs.
exercises.mistake: Don't lock your knee; keep it slightly soft.

exercises.name: Step Calf Raise
exercises.setup: Stand with the balls of your feet on the edge of a step, heels hanging off. Support yourself with one hand on a wall or railing.
steps: Let your heels drop below the level of the step; feel the stretch in your calves.
Rise up onto your toes.
Slowly lower back down.
exercises.tip: The stretched part at the bottom is the part that helps most.
exercises.mistake: Keep half your foot on the step so you don't slip off.

exercises.name: Slow-Lowering Calf Raise
exercises.setup: Stand with the balls of your feet on the edge of a step, holding on with one hand.
steps: Rise quickly onto your toes on both feet.
Lower your heel slowly over 4 seconds, on one foot if you can.
Rise again on both feet and repeat.
exercises.tip: There may be mild discomfort on the way down; stop if there's sharp pain.
exercises.mistake: Don't rush the lowering; the real work is in the slow descent.

exercises.name: Tiptoe Hold
exercises.setup: Stand up and support yourself with one hand on a wall.
steps: Rise up onto your toes.
Stay at the top; don't let your heels drop.
Keep breathing and hold until the time is up.
exercises.mistake: Don't let yourself sink by bending your knees.

exercises.name: Bent-Knee Calf Raise
exercises.setup: Stand, bend your knees slightly and keep that angle. Reach your arms forward for balance.
steps: Lift your heels while keeping your knees bent.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Keep the knee angle the same throughout the move.
exercises.mistake: Don't straighten your knees as you rise.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.setup: Sit upright on a chair, feet on the floor, hands on your knees.
steps: Lift your heels off the floor.
Pause briefly at the top; you can make it harder by pressing down on your knees with your hands.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Putting a heavy bag on your knees makes the move harder.
exercises.mistake: Don't do it fast and bouncy.

exercises.name: Pogo Hops
exercises.target: Calves and Achilles tendon (elasticity and power)
exercises.setup: Stand on your toes, feet hip-width apart.
steps: Bend your knees very slightly, spring from your ankles and do small hops.
Land softly on your toes.
Keep going in rhythm without your heels touching the floor.
exercises.tip: Spend little time on the ground; bounce like a spring.
exercises.mistake: Don't do it if you have pain in your Achilles tendon.

exercises.name: Imaginary Jump Rope
exercises.setup: Stand on your toes with your hands beside your hips as if holding a rope.
steps: Do small jumps while drawing small circles with your wrists.
Land softly on your toes.
Keep the rhythm and continue.
exercises.tip: If you have a real rope, you can use that too.
exercises.mistake: Don't jump high; a few centimetres is enough.

exercises.name: Wall Toe Raise
exercises.setup: Lean your back against a wall and place your feet one step in front of it.
steps: Keep your heels on the floor and lift the front of your feet.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Because it balances the calves, it may help runners against shin pain.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your hips come away from the wall.

exercises.name: Wall Calf Stretch
exercises.setup: Face a wall and put your hands on it. One foot forward, the other a step behind.
steps: Keep the back leg straight and the heel on the floor.
Bend your front knee and move your body towards the wall.
Feel the stretch in your back calf and hold; switch legs halfway through.
exercises.tip: Bending the back knee slightly stretches the lower calf.

exercises.name: Downward-Dog Pedal
exercises.target: Calves and back of the legs (stretch)
exercises.setup: Hands and feet on the floor, hips up high; your body like an upside-down V.
steps: Bend one knee and press the other heel towards the floor.
Switch sides.
Keep going slowly, as if pedalling.
exercises.tip: It's fine if your heels don't touch the floor.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your shoulders sink; keep pushing the floor away with your hands.
